en.title: Integer to Decimal String
en.description:
Implement conversion from an integer to a decimal string without using built-in number-to-string functions. Output one line for each signed 32-bit integer in the input; negative numbers keep the minus sign, and 0 is output as 0.

The upstream original problem forbids a built-in conversion helper; this site's judge can only verify the output and cannot statically prove that a contestant did not call a built-in conversion function.

This site's standard input/output protocol was explicitly added by CSWork and does not mean the upstream function-style problem originally had this protocol.
en.input: Each line contains one signed 32-bit integer; there are 1..100000 lines. The last line of input may or may not end with a newline.
en.output: Output one line with the decimal representation of each input integer.
en.explanation: Process according to the rules; see the accompanying editorial for the approach, proof of correctness and complexity.
hints: Repeatedly take the last digit of the absolute value and divide by 10, join the digits in reverse order, and finally add a minus sign if needed. Handle 0 separately. To cover INT_MIN, use an integer representation that does not overflow.
